label: Terrazzo · epoxy (dark charcoal matrix, white/grey marble chips + pores)

source.selection_reason: Owner-curated macro of a DARK charcoal terrazzo slab — black/anthracite matrix with white and grey marble chips plus characteristic vesicular pores. Already flat and face-on at very high resolution (7168x4096). Exactly the dark epoxy-terrazzo look this slug represents.
source.crop_reason: 3500px square from the central-left flat area, avoiding the slightly brighter top-right corner so the de-light has the least gradient to remove. Even chip + pore distribution, no edges.
source.rejected_set: The white/multicolour DNA tile is terrazzo-multi; the grey cement-concrete macros are terrazzo-cement / decorative-concrete.

material_truth.fillers: White + grey marble/natural-stone chips (~4-15 mm) set in a dark matrix, with abundant small vesicular pores (air voids characteristic of cast terrazzo). One sparse warm fleck visible.
material_truth.matrix: Charcoal/anthracite matrix (near-black cement or pigmented epoxy).
material_truth.finish: Ground + sealed, satin-to-semi-polished. Visible micro-relief from pores and chip edges.
material_truth.manufacturer_recipe: Epoxy-terrazzo (e.g. Decodur EP-Terrazzo / Sikafloor epoxy-terrazzo) with charcoal-pigmented binder and white/grey marble broadcast 4-15 mm, ground and PU-sealed to satin; or a dark cement terrazzo (Sikafloor Terrazzo CS-31, charcoal pigment).

colour.note: High-contrast surface (stdev ~41) — bright marble chips over a dark matrix. The 'matrix' hex is sampled from the heavily-blurred median (kills chips) and reads as a dark neutral charcoal; overall mean #414142 sits a touch darker because pores/black matrix dominate area.

scale.physical_mm_per_tile: ~150-200 mm represented by the 2048px master (macro shot; chips read ~4-15 mm at this crop).
scale.tile_note: Manifest 'tile' is an integer repeat. 5 keeps the chips at a realistic 4-15 mm read on a ~600-900 mm plate. Do NOT drop below 3 (chips would look oversized).

gloss.note: Semi-polished dark terrazzo. roughness.png mean is 0.601 because gen-pbr's chipsSmooth formula maps the large dark-matrix area to higher roughness; the bright chips correctly read smoother. For a polished epoxy-terrazzo look, recommend a roughness_override scalar ~0.30-0.38 (the map still provides the chip/matrix contrast). Use ~0.35.

normal.png.strength: gen-pbr bump 5.0 (per-chip + pore relief); R range 0-254

processing.decode: sharp JPG -> extract 3500px square -> lanczos3 DOWNSCALE to 2048 (sharp, no upscaling).
processing.delight: sharp divide-by-heavy-blur (sigma scaled to ~144px) re-multiplied by per-channel means -> removed the mild corner gradient, lighting-neutral albedo.
processing.seamless: Half-offset (quadrant-swap) wrap + feathered cross-fade heal blending with a 180°-rotated copy of the offset. The high-frequency chip+pore field hides the wrap completely. Validated by 2x2 tiling (no seam, no obvious repeat).
processing.pbr: scripts/gen-pbr-maps.js terrazzo-epoxy --root=3d-assets/textures-v4 (bump 5.0, baseRough 0.4, chipsSmooth true, ao 1.2).

caveats: Not upscaled — downscaled from a 3500px crop; this is the sharpest of the four masters.
One faint warm speck (a sensor/dust mote in the source macro) sits near the centre-right; negligible at render scale.
roughness.png mean (0.601) reads rougher than a polished terrazzo; prefer the recommended roughness_override scalar (~0.35) over the raw map mean if a semi-polished sheen is desired.
Dark matrix means the configurator colour control should be used cautiously — tinting a near-black albedo has limited range.

recommended_manifest.palette_note: matrix charcoal, overall mean, white marble chip, light-grey chip, near-black pore, mid-grey chip
recommended_manifest.note: Repoint pbr.* to textures-v4/terrazzo-epoxy/* to use this new set. New slug folder — was not present before. (Orchestrator applies — do not edit manifest here.)
